title: state set feature swap closes other live workflow records
action: PBI p-71d014e7, narrowed by verification: start-feature already reaps — policy.rs:684-697 calls ensure_workflow_record_for_feature then close_workflows_for_feature (feature.rs:390-406). But `state set --feature <swap>` takes a different path: ledger.rs:291-329 write_through_projection — a feature swap deliberately falls to the C1 direct write_state fallback (comment ledger.rs:301-305), leaving the OLD feature's live workflow record orphaned (found via find_live_workflow), exactly what the PBI describes. Fix: on the set --feature swap path (the real seam may be in set_gate.rs's state-set handler or around the C1 fallback — declared files are hypotheses, follow the real site and name it), after the state write succeeds, close every OTHER live workflow record and ensure the incoming feature's record — reuse close_workflows_for_feature and ensure_workflow_record_for_feature exactly as policy.rs does, never a second implementation. The C1 carve-out's own write behavior stays byte-identical; only the orphan-reap rides after it. A swap to the SAME feature is a no-op for the reap. TDD red-first: fixture with a live workflow record for feature A -> state set --feature B: A's record is closed (terminal), B has a record; same-feature set changes nothing; the existing swap-door tests stay green.

truths: a feature swap via state set leaves zero orphaned live workflow records
the incoming feature has a record after the swap
the C1 direct-write behavior itself is byte-identical

artifacts.substantive: reap wiring plus tests (or the real seam, named in the trace)

trace.outcome: state set feature swap reaps: outgoing workflow record closed, incoming ensured, via the same feature.rs functions start-feature uses; C1 direct write byte-identical; real seam run_set_body
